assign.outcome:
**The loop closes** — the world at `/imagine/game/` now has an ending, a fourth verb and a map. Round 1 was extended; nothing was rebuilt.

![](game2-7-finale-1920.png)

- [/imagine/game/](/imagine/game/) — **the arrival, rewritten as an opening**: eyebrow, display line, one accent rule, one lede, in one capped centred composition. The ramp it buys — block `328 / 517 / 618 / 696`, display type `36 / 57 / 68 / 77px` at 400 / 1280 / 1920 / 3440.
- [/imagine/game/end/](/imagine/game/end/) — **the ending**. One real page, two states: the shut gate while the sigil is in the Vault, the finale once it is in your pack. A rail row from the first paint, so the run always has somewhere to be going — and the only eraser.
- **The mechanic: a trade.** The Keeper in the Long Gallery wants the brass lamp and holds a ground lens — the only move that *shrinks* the pack. One click moves two rail rows in opposite directions: Cistern `walked` → `needs the brass lamp`, Lantern Room `needs the ground lens` → `unwalked`. She will not deal until you carry the key, which is the only thing between a player and a run that cannot be finished.
- **The map**, in the run rail, always on screen. Nine cells and three labels in one grid; a walked room is an `<a>`, an unwalked one is a `<span>` and cannot be clicked — the rule is which element gets built, so it cannot drift.
- [/imagine/game/readme/](/imagine/game/readme/) — the index · [`doc/decisions.md`](/imagine/game/doc/decisions.md) — the record: why a trade and not a shortcut, the anti-softlock guard, the measurements, what was cut.

**Measured** (headless, a full run start → vault → finale, one shot per beat). Finale tiles `9/9 | 3/3 | 3 | 1 | lit`; the store held nine `found`, three `carried`, one `traded` and `spire/lantern` walked — identical, because there is one source. Map links vs `found.length` at every beat: `0/0, 2/2, 5/5, 6/6, 9/9`, and `0/0` after *start over*. *Start over* removed `lew42:/imagine/game/` and left `lew42:/imagine/team/` standing. Reload mid-run: store byte-identical, finale still drawn, nine map links. 15 urls crawled in both states, **zero console errors and no overflow at 400 / 1280 / 1920 / 3440**.

**Cut** — the rail's `reset run` button (two erasers is two devices saying one thing; the finale is the eraser and the rail's room went to the map) · `preview()` cards as the map (nine 15em cards do not fit a 14em rail, and a preview is *a picture, never a live instance* — the map redraws on every move) · a second, larger map on the arrival · `fill` for the two written screens (at 3440 a `large` column caps at 1152px and the row ends 1984px short of the viewport — but `fill` moves that emptiness *inside* the column, and a 2632px sheet of paper holding a 40em paragraph is worse).

`store.js` was **not** touched: `clear()` already existed and the game needed nothing else, so the storage-not-state verdict in its readme still holds.

**Left:** the 3440 gutter is core's width word doing what it says, not this section's to fix. Every readme route probes for a `page.js` first and 404s in console (`/imagine/readme/` does it twice) — pre-existing, out of fence.
